sections.body: All living things are made of CELLS. Animal and plant cells have a nucleus, cytoplasm and a membrane. Plant cells also have a cell wall and chloroplasts.
The nucleus holds DNA, which is organised into GENES: instructions for building and running the body. Offspring inherit genes from their parents.
EVOLUTION by NATURAL SELECTION: individuals vary; those with traits better suited to their environment tend to survive and reproduce more, so those traits become more common over many generations.
Scientists CLASSIFY living things into groups (kingdom → species) based on shared features and DNA.

quiz.q: Which structure do plant cells have but animal cells don't?
hints: Both cell types have a nucleus and membrane. The extra part in plants is green…
quiz.explain: Chloroplasts (for photosynthesis) are found in plant cells, not animal cells.

quiz.q: In a snowy area, white rabbits are caught less by predators than brown ones. Over many generations, what happens?
hints: Which rabbits survive to have babies?
Their genes get passed on more.
Moths that match tree bark get eaten less, so bark-coloured moths become more common.
quiz.explain: White rabbits survive and reproduce more, so white fur becomes more common: natural selection.

options: Sections of DNA that carry instructions for building and running the body
Tiny structures that make food from sunlight
The outer layer that controls what enters and leaves a cell
hints: Genes are part of something that the nucleus holds.
The lesson calls them a kind of 'instructions'. The other two options describe cell parts from the first paragraph.
A recipe book holds many recipes, and each one tells a cook how to make one dish. If DNA is the book, what are the recipes?
quiz.explain: DNA in the nucleus is organised into genes: instructions for building and running the body. Making food from sunlight is the job of chloroplasts, and the membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell.
